rationale: submittedAsync described async queuing of the request; the only candidate invalidFields holds field validation errors, an unrelated piece of information.
submittedAsync is an async-processing flag; accountCode and invalidFields carry unrelated information, so it was dropped in v5.
submittedAsync is a processing-mode flag; the only candidate primaryCurrency is an unrelated ISO currency code, so the flag was simply dropped.
submittedAsync is dropped from the response; the added fields are payout settings, metadata and invalidFields, none of which describes asynchronous processing.
submittedAsync (async processing flag) has no counterpart among the candidates, which are validation errors, migration data, a freshness timestamp and new per-account settings.
Same int32 type and same description (the check code), renamed alongside description becoming kycCheckDescription.
KYCCheckSummary renamed both fields in v5: code became kycCheckCode and description became kycCheckDescription with an identical description and type.
updatedFields (list of fields changed by the request) has no counterpart; the only addition, primaryCurrency, is an unrelated currency code.

The bank account check results were keyed by bankAccountUUID; the new payoutMethods results are keyed by payoutMethodCode and match the removed cards results instead, and no other candidate covers bank accounts.
The cards item schema had payoutMethodCode plus checks, and KYCPayoutMethodCheckResult has exactly the same two properties, so card check results became payout method check results.
Contact no longer exists in the new spec; personalData held date of birth and ID style data, which none of the address line candidates carry.

Left out: a reader could not settle it. First reader: Contact became DeliveryContact whose address now uses Address-2 with free-form line1/line2/line3 instead of street plus houseNumberOrName; which line carries the house number is not determined by the spec. Second reader: The Contact schema is absent from the new spec; the new Address-2 uses line1/line2/line3 instead of street plus houseNumberOrName, but nothing states which line the house number or name now goes into, so the mapping is not decisive.

The Contact schema became DeliveryContact (same deliveryContact refs on Card and CardInfo) and its address moved from a street/houseNumberOrName structure to line1/line2/line3, so the street now goes in the first address line.

The v2 redesign moved rule conditions into ruleRestrictions; the old maximum amount per interval is now expressed by ruleRestrictions.totalAmount with an operation, alongside countries, mccs, entryModes and processingTypes.

The new required entityKey object holds entityType (with balancePlatform as a value) plus entityReference, replacing the separate balancePlatformId, paymentInstrumentId and paymentInstrumentGroupId targets.
In v2 the rule conditions moved into ruleRestrictions (TransactionRuleRestrictions), which has a countries restriction object with value list and operation.
The new TransactionRuleRestrictions object behind ruleRestrictions has an entryModes condition, and the other flat conditions (countries, mccs, processingTypes) moved there in the same release.
The maximum transaction count per interval is now expressed by ruleRestrictions.matchingTransactions (a count plus an operation), part of the same move of conditions into ruleRestrictions.
The new ruleRestrictions object has an mccs entry (MccsRestriction with a value list of MCCs plus an operation), so the MCC list moved inside it.
v2 replaces the per-resource id fields with entityKey {entityType, entityReference}, and entityType explicitly lists paymentInstrumentGroup.

entityKey holds entityType (which includes paymentInstrument) plus entityReference, replacing the flat paymentInstrumentId, paymentInstrumentGroupId and balancePlatformId targets that were all removed.
TransactionRuleRestrictions has a processingTypes restriction (list plus operation), so the old top-level list moved inside ruleRestrictions.
The single 3D Secure version string was replaced by an array of supported 3D Secure protocol versions in the same schema.
authResponse was an authorisation code for the authentication result; the added authentication map holds threeds2 fingerprint or challengeToken inputs for further calls, a different piece of data.
supportsRecurring was a tokenization support flag; the only candidate, brand, is the gift card brand and carries no such information.
action was a oneOf of CheckoutRedirectAction only; threeDS2ResponseData holds 3DS2 ACS response data and threeDSPaymentData a token string, neither carries the redirect action.

authentication was already deprecated in favour of action; the new threeDS2ResponseData holds ARes fields (acsTransID, transStatus, etc.) and threeDSPaymentData is a paymentData value, neither carries the fingerprint or challengeToken map.

details (list of input fields to submit) is dropped along with action and paymentData; threeDSPaymentData parallels the removed paymentData, and threeDS2ResponseData is 3DS2 response data, neither replaces the details field list.
outputDetails was deprecated with a pointer to action, which was removed too; the new 3DS2 response data and threeDSPaymentData fields do not carry the shopper-facing output details.

Both are strings with near-identical descriptions (a value to submit to /payments/details), the new one explicitly as paymentData; paymentData was deprecated and removed in the same release that added threeDSPaymentData.
redirect was deprecated in favour of action and is dropped; the 3DS2 response data object and the paymentData string are different information.
The boolean storePaymentMethod is replaced by the enum storePaymentMethodMode (disabled, askForConsent, enabled) describing the same storing of payment details for the shopperReference.

Left out: a reader could not settle it. First reader: details was a generic list of input details, and the new issuers list covers only the issuer select list that details used to carry for some methods, so the replacement is partial and not decisive. Second reader: details was a generic InputDetail array; the new issuers array (id, name, disabled) covers only the issuer-selection part of it, and the identical deprecated inputDetails array remains, so it is unclear whether issuers counts as its successor.
Identical description of the reason for the amount update with the same enum values plus one added value (installment).
submittedAsync is a processing-mode flag; invalidFields (validation errors) and payoutSpeed (payout speed) are unrelated additions.
DnsServiceDiscovery's only field serviceName became hostname, both describing the DNS name used for the virtual node's service discovery.
serviceNames associated mesh service names with the router, while listeners describe port mappings for inbound traffic; service names moved to separate virtual service resources, not into listeners.
serviceNames associated mesh service names, while listeners describe port mappings for inbound traffic; the service association moved to virtual services, not to listeners or tags.
The virtual router spec dropped its service name list; listeners describes port mappings for inbound traffic, a different concept.
The document count is not carried over; ARN is an identifier and Limits holds replication and partition maximums.
The uint field type was replaced by int in the IndexFieldType enum, and IntOptions has the same role of per-type options with DefaultValue, now a 64-bit signed integer.

The source mapping and transformation functions were dropped; source selection is now a SourceField inside each type-specific options object, including pre-existing TextOptions and LiteralOptions, so no single candidate replaced it.
LiteralOptions keeps Search and Facet flags; ResultEnabled (returnable in search results) maps to ReturnEnabled with the same meaning, while SortEnabled and SourceField are new capabilities.
The 2013 TextOptions has no facet setting at all; the added flags cover return, sort and highlight, and ReturnEnabled corresponds to the removed ResultEnabled, not FacetEnabled.
ResultEnabled (values can be returned in search results) was renamed ReturnEnabled with the same boolean meaning, while the other candidates cover sorting, highlighting and analysis.

The old field named the text processor to apply (cs_text_no_stemming to disable stemming); in the 2013 API text analysis such as stemming is configured by naming an analysis scheme for the text field.
Responses was a map of table name to consumed capacity units; ConsumedCapacity carries the same per-table capacity as an array of TableName and CapacityUnits entries.
The scalar ConsumedCapacityUnits is replaced by the ConsumedCapacity object, which contains CapacityUnits plus per-table and per-index breakdowns.
The scalar capacity units figure is now reported inside the ConsumedCapacity object, which carries the total capacity units consumed plus per-table and per-index detail.
AttributeType (String or Number) moved to table-level AttributeDefinitions; KeyType is the HASH or RANGE role, which was previously implied by the key element position.
The Count boolean was replaced by the Select enum, whose COUNT value requests the number of matching items instead of the items.

Left out: a reader could not settle it. First reader: HashKeyValue is superseded by key conditions, but the new spec offers both the legacy KeyConditions map and KeyConditionExpression with ExpressionAttributeValues, so more than one candidate carries the hash key value. Second reader: In the 2012-08-10 API the separate HashKeyValue and RangeKeyCondition parameters were merged into the KeyConditions map of key attribute conditions; the hash key value is now its EQ condition (KeyConditionExpression is a later expression-based alternative).
The 2012 API replaced HashKeyValue and RangeKeyCondition with the KeyConditions map of attribute conditions, which holds the range key condition.
The consumed capacity unit count is now reported inside the ConsumedCapacity object (its CapacityUnits member), with extra per-index detail.
The Count boolean was replaced by the Select enum, whose COUNT value requests the item count instead of the items.
Pure casing rename of the function ARN field with matching description.

Left out: a reader could not settle it. First reader: ConfigurationId identified the code plus configuration; CodeSha256, Version and RevisionId each overlap partly but none is clearly the same identifier. Second reader: ConfigurationId identified the current code and configuration; no candidate is clearly the same, though RevisionId (latest revision of the function) is conceptually close while CodeSha256 and Version cover only parts.
Mode was the upload type of the function (event); none of the added fields (ARN, versions, VPC, state, package type etc.) carries that value.
The single OptionGroupMembership object became the OptionGroupMemberships array in the same DBInstance schema, a pluralisation of the same data.
v1beta has no egress policy concept; unrestrictedServices is an unrelated deprecated service wildcard list.
ingressPolicies are access rules for the perimeter; unrestrictedServices is a deprecated wildcard list of unrestricted services, unrelated.
Each servingRestrictions entry has a disapprovalReasons array with the same item shape (reason, details), so the reasons moved into per-context restriction entries.

Left out: a reader could not settle it. First reader: The single serving status was split into openAuctionStatus and dealsStatus (plus granular servingRestrictions), so no single candidate is clearly its successor. Second reader: Single serving status was split into dealsStatus and openAuctionStatus (plus servingRestrictions); no single candidate is clearly its successor.
creation_time (int64 timestamp) is re-encoded as createTime, a google-datetime described as the creation time of the account.
The account ID now lives in the resource name, which already existed as a field (it was the display name in v1.4); none of the candidates carries the ID.
The kind discriminator was dropped in the v2 API; the added fields carry other data.
subAccounts is not represented by any candidate; the v2 Account only has display, state, time and task fields.
The string timezone became the TimeZone object timeZone, whose id holds the IANA zone of the account.
etag was a response caching tag; the accounts candidate is the renamed items list, not the etag.
Same description (the accounts returned in this list response), array of Account, renamed from items.
kind is a type marker dropped in v2; the list moved from items to accounts, which is not the kind information.
ARC opt-in status has no successor; the added fields are resource name, reporting id and a readiness state.

Left out: a reader could not settle it. First reader: The ad client ID is now carried both by the new resource name and by reportingDimensionId, so which candidate is its successor is ambiguous. The kind discriminator was dropped in the v2 API; name, reportingDimensionId and state carry other data.

Left out: a reader could not settle it. The response etag is dropped; adClients is the renamed items list, not the etag.
Same list of AdClient objects with an identical description, renamed from items to adClients in v2.
The kind discriminator was dropped; adClients replaced the items list, not kind.

Left out: a reader could not settle it. Second reader: The ad unit code is the short identifier now embedded in the resource name (an existing field) and possibly in reportingDimensionId; evidence is not decisive.
contentAdsSettings is kept but its backupOption is dropped; the added fields are displayName, reportingDimensionId and state, unrelated to backup ads.
customStyle held ad styling; the candidates are display name, reporting ID and state, and v2 has no style information.
Deprecated feed ads settings were dropped; displayName, reportingDimensionId and state are unrelated.

Left out: a reader could not settle it. First reader: The opaque unique id could have become reportingDimensionId or be carried by the kept, repurposed name field; the spec gives no example values to decide. Second reader: The opaque unique id could correspond to reportingDimensionId or to the resource name (an existing field that changed meaning); not decisive.
The kind discriminator was dropped in v2; no candidate carries a resource kind string.
mobileContentAdsSettings was deprecated WAP ad settings and was dropped in v2; none of the candidates relates to it.
The saved style reference was dropped in v2; none of the added fields refers to styles.

Left out: a reader could not settle it. First reader: state replaces status in the same slot but the enums differ in meaning (activity based NEW/ACTIVE/INACTIVE versus lifecycle ACTIVE/ARCHIVED), so it is not clearly the same information. Same position in the header object, same condition (only for METRIC_CURRENCY), now named currencyCode and described as an ISO-4217 code.
kind was a constant resource type marker dropped in v2; a header currency code is unrelated.
The old opaque alert id is replaced by the resource name accounts/{account}/alerts/{alert}, which is now the alert's identifier; the old schema had no name field.
isDismissible has no counterpart; the only candidate name is the alert resource name.
The kind discriminator was dropped in v2; name is a resource path, not a kind string.
Same list of Alert objects with an identical description, renamed from items to alerts.
The kind discriminator was dropped; alerts replaced the items list, not kind.

Left out: a reader could not settle it. Left out: a reader could not settle it. Payment lost its id and gained a resource name whose last segment identifies the payment (unpaid or a payment date); amount and date replace the other removed fields.

paymentAmount and its currency code were merged into amount, a formatted string that includes the currency.

Left out: a reader could not settle it. First reader: The opaque unique id could map to the resource name or to reportingDimensionId; both are plausible and the spec does not disambiguate. In androidpublisher v3 versionCodes (and userFraction) moved into each TrackRelease in the releases array.
pendingManagedCertificateId is the ID of a certificate being provisioned; isManagedCertificate is a boolean about the mapped certificate, different information.

proof_of_registration was a document upload (files and signer); the candidates are company address objects, and the document type was simply removed.
dynamic_tax_rates was removed from line items; the candidates are setup_future_usage options for unrelated payment methods.

Schema renamed to ApplicationLastDataAccessTimes with the timestamps renamed to the data scope names; contact_info has the identical last-accessed description and credit_and_loans likewise became credit_loan_info.

The schema was renamed ApplicationLastDataAccessTimes and its per-scope timestamps were renamed to the data scope names, with credit_and_loans becoming credit_loan_info (same type, format and description pattern).
payroll_info and transaction_risk_info were dropped from the access-times schema; contact_info and credit_loan_info are renames of contact_details and credit_and_loans, other data types.

The schema was renamed to ApplicationLastDataAccessTimes and transaction_risk_info and payroll_info were dropped; contact_info and credit_loan_info are renames of contact_details and credit_and_loans.
Protect Session ID was renamed Device Session ID consistently across Protect schemas in this release, with otherwise identical descriptions.

The response changed from a full conversation to a participants list; the conversation id is not carried by customers.

Same description and type, the parameter was renamed with a Transcription prefix.

Within each dimension title was replaced by displayName in the same position and type, alongside the matching change for measures.
identity (participant identity) was dropped from transcriptions; configuration is a layout or settings object, unrelated.
The list response key was corrected from extensions to transcriptions, with the same item schema and the meta key changing to match.
Referencing an existing Participant by participantId is dropped; profileId points to a Profile, a different resource, and the other candidates are new roster attributes.
The single channel-specific address string became an addresses array of objects each holding channel and the same formatted address.
The flat request was replaced by a participant roster plus a typed action; the channel now lives in the SEND_MESSAGE action's channel field, and VOICE became the CALL action type.

Left out: a reader could not settle it. Left out: a reader could not settle it. Message content now goes in the SEND_MESSAGE action payload (action.payload.content, same send_content schema) rather than a top-level content field.
The same channel_settings schema now sits in the SEND_MESSAGE action payload (action.payload.channelSettings).

Left out: a reader could not settle it. Left out: a reader could not settle it. Case change of the same field, identical description.
